title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin and trabectedin
schedule_label: Two infusions on day 1 every three weeks.
schedule_summary: You receive a steroid before pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, followed by trabectedin over three hours. Your team normally recommends a central line. Treatment repeats every 21 days while it helps and remains tolerable.
purpose: Control relapsed disease and delay further progression.
administration_text: You receive a steroid before pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, followed by trabectedin over three hours. Your team normally recommends a central line. Treatment repeats every 21 days while it helps and remains tolerable.
monitoring_summary: Check creatine kinase weekly for the first two cycles. Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.explanation: A coated carrier delivers doxorubicin, which damages DNA. Prior anthracycline exposure matters for heart safety.
agents.mechanism: A coated carrier delivers doxorubicin, which damages DNA. Prior anthracycline exposure matters for heart safety.
agents.watch: Report sore palms or soles, mouth ulcers, ankle swelling or breathlessness.
visual: A coated carrier delivers doxorubicin, which damages DNA. Prior anthracycline exposure matters for heart safety.

agents.name: Trabectedin
agents.explanation: It binds to DNA and disrupts processes that tumour cells need to grow.
agents.mechanism: It binds to DNA and disrupts processes that tumour cells need to grow.
agents.watch: Severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine needs urgent assessment.
visual: It binds to DNA and disrupts processes that tumour cells need to grow.

common_effects.title: How you feel between visits
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea or appetite changes can make everyday activities harder. Ask your team for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Hand and foot soreness · Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
serious_effects.text: Report painful redness, peeling or blisters before the next cycle.

serious_effects.title: Heart problems · Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
serious_effects.text: Report new breathlessness, ankle swelling or difficulty lying flat.

serious_effects.title: Muscle injury · Trabectedin
serious_effects.text: Report severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine immediately.

serious_effects.title: Liver injury · Trabectedin
serious_effects.text: Report jaundice, dark urine or marked fatigue urgently.

questions.q: What happens at my next visit?
questions.a: Two infusions on day 1 every three weeks.

questions.q: Which symptoms should I phone about?
questions.a: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shivering or sudden illness. Call urgently for severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.

questions.q: What should I plan before starting?
questions.a: Bring details of earlier anthracyclines and heart problems.

evidence.title: OVA-301
evidence.interpretation: Adding trabectedin to liposomal doxorubicin delayed progression compared with liposomal doxorubicin alone.
evidence.limitations: The trial does not compare this combination directly with retreatment using platinum.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, bilirubin, liver enzymes, albumin, kidney function, creatine kinase and heart function.
Bring details of earlier anthracyclines and heart problems.

rows.label: First two cycles
cells: Check creatine kinase weekly for the first two cycles. Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle.
Ask for the dates of blood tests between infusions.

rows.label: Before later cycles
cells: Check creatine kinase at least once between later cycles. ECG and heart assessment by ECHO or MUGA are part of monitoring. ECHO or MUGA is due before every cycle.
Report muscle pain with weakness or dark urine urgently.

monitoring_schedule.note: Scan dates and tumour-marker testing are individualised by your oncology team.
